results.title: Social expectations, political financing threaten judicial integrity – Valentin Kwasi Mensah
results.content: Governance specialist Valentin Kwasi Mensah has warned that social expectations and political financing can undermine judicial impartiality in Ghana, arguing that threats to the independence of public officials extend beyond direct political interference. Speaking at a JoyNews public lecture on the theme “Even Judges Must Eat – An Outside-In Provocation,” Mr Mensah said public officials often face demands from relatives, friends, former schoolmates, religious communities and political supporters that could influence their decisions. “Requests for preferential treatment often arrive as appeals to loyalty or gratitude,” he said.

results.title: Governance specialist calls for digital reforms to improve justice delivery
results.content: Governance specialist Valentin Kwasi Mensah has called for greater transparency in judicial appointments and sustained investment in technology to improve justice delivery, citing declining public confidence in Ghana’s courts. Speaking at a JoyNews public lecture on the theme “Even Judges Must Eat – An Outside-In Provocation,” Mr Mensah cited Afrobarometer’s 2024 survey, which found that 35% of Ghanaians trusted the courts somewhat or a lot, down from 57% in 2017. He said the figures highlighted the need for reforms that would strengthen accountability and demonstrate fairness in the administration of justice.

results.title: Nacee announces star-studded second edition of KAVOD for November 8
results.content: Award-winning musician, song writer and record producer Nacee is preparing to stage the second edition of his entertainment event, KAVOD 26, at the National Theatre in Accra on Sunday, November 8, 2026.

results.title: Fund judiciary adequately to protect judicial independence – Valentin Mensah
results.content: Governance specialist Valentin Kwasi Mensah has called for adequate funding and resources for Ghana’s judiciary, arguing that judicial independence cannot be guaranteed without the financial and material capacity to deliver justice. Speaking at a JoyNews public lecture on the theme “Even Judges Must Eat – An Outside-In Provocation,” Mr Mensah said judges could be independent in principle but struggle to perform their duties effectively if courts lacked adequate staff, functional computers and operational funds. “Even judges must eat captures an important truth. Judges and court workers need decent conditions, while courts need buildings, records, equipment and functioning systems. Independence requires the means to do the work,” he said.

results.title: Ghana–New Zealand Chamber seeks tourism partnerships between the two countries
results.content: The Ghana-New Zealand Chamber of Commerce is exploring opportunities to strengthen tourism and business ties between Ghana and New Zealand by connecting tourism operators, guides and industry stakeholders in both countries.

results.title: Binduri Naaba urges EPA to prosecute violators of Styrofoam ban
results.content: The Binduri Naaba, Alhaji Akorlbila Agetwin Robert, has called on the Environmental Protection Authority (EPA) to prosecute individuals and businesses that violate Ghana’s impending ban on Styrofoam products, insisting that strict enforcement is essential to securing compliance.

results.content: The Tema Regional Police Command has arrested a 52-year-old man, Ibrahim Saani, for allegedly possessing 37 parcels of substances suspected to be Indian hemp at New York, near Airport Junction.

results.title: Road crashes drop by 9.4% following TraffiTech sensitisation – MTTD
results.content: The Director of Education, Research and Training at the Police Motor Traffic and Transport Department (MTTD), ACP Alexander Kwaku Obeng, says road crashes reported across Ghana declined by 9.4% following intensified sensitisation and caution notices issued to motorists under the TraffiTech-GH pilot project.

results.title: YAWC Network calls for revocation of licences of teachers convicted of sexual abuse
results.content: The Executive Director of the Young African Women Congress (YAWC) Network, Daniel Osei Tuffour, has called for the revocation of the teaching licences of teachers found guilty of sexually abusing students, arguing that transferring offenders to other schools is not enough to protect children. He has urged the Ghana Education Service (GES) and other relevant authorities to impose stricter sanctions on teachers who commit sexual offences against students, including prosecution and the withdrawal of their professional licences. Mr Tuffour made the call at the YAWC Network’s 10th anniversary celebration in Accra on Monday, October 26.

results.title: NPP heads to Supreme Court over interpretation of presidential limit
results.content: The New Patriotic Party (NPP) has filed a suit at the Supreme Court seeking an interpretation of the constitutional provisions governing presidential term limits, in a case that could determine whether President John Dramani Mahama is eligible to seek another term in office in 2028. The writ of summons and statement of case, dated July 28, 2026, were filed by the party’s solicitor, Godfred Yeboah Dame of Dame & Partners, with the Attorney-General named as the defendant. The party is asking the court to clarify whether the constitutional limit of two presidential terms applies regardless of whether the terms are served consecutively or are separated by a period out of office.

results.title: John Darko calls for stronger women’s representation in Parliament
results.content: The Member of Parliament for Suame, John Darko, has called for greater representation of women in Parliament and other leadership positions, warning that their underrepresentation limits the range of perspectives shaping national decisions. Speaking at an event organised by the Young African Women Congress Network (YAWC Network) in Accra on Monday, October 26, he said Ghana was missing out on the skills, experience and ideas women could contribute to national development. “A democracy that excludes women from meaningful participation in political and economic decision-making deprives itself of the competence, experiences and perspectives of substantial portions of its citizens,” he said.
